Subject: Post-call: performance acceptance criteria & measurement (Acme Retail)

Hi Sam — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and the action items we discussed so both sides have the same expectations before we draft SLA language.

Call summary (high level):
- Objective: Ensure Redwood will meet Acme’s interactive personalization latency and throughput needs for peak shopping hours (US East peak).
- Workloads discussed: short text generation (catalog/title suggestions) and streaming token previews for realtime personalization widgets.

Qual targets we captured (please confirm):
- Non-streaming text generation: p95 server-side latency <= 250 ms for requests <= 512 tokens.
- Streaming token latency: under 100 ms first-byte-to-client at p95 for streamed token delivery when using our streaming API/config.
- Sustained throughput: 600 qps across the fleet for catalog generation (across 4 regions) with concurrency target of 200 concurrent request contexts per region.
- Burst behavior: support short bursts up to 1,000 qps for <5 min windows during flash sales (best-effort with autoscale).

Measurement & reporting notes we discussed:
- Measurement window: rolling 5-minute buckets; p95 computed on the server processing time (end-to-end server token generation) excluding client-side rendering and last-mile network variability.
- Exclusions: planned maintenance windows (>=30m) with notice, controlled bulk batch jobs (customer-initiation >5k parallel requests flagged in traffic map), and force majeure.
- Reporting cadence: weekly automated report + monthly SLA summary dashboard; immediate incident reports for any >2% breach over a 24h period.

Suggested next steps (for this week):
1) Sam: share a 24–72 hour traffic sample (CSV) and peak window timestamps so we can validate our sizing against real distributions (attachment: acme-maP-traffic-patterns.csv).
2) Redwood: share a draft SLA language (attached) with explicit measurement method, exclusions, and tiered remedy schedule (attachment: proposed-sla-draft.pdf).
3) Scheduling: set up a 60–90 minute technical runbook review with Acme infra + Redwood infra (we suggested Tue/Thu next week).

Attachments: proposed-sla-draft.pdf; acme-maP-traffic-patterns.csv (sample format).

Thanks — I’ll wait for the traffic sample and will refine the SLA draft once we see the distribution.

Thanks Sam — good questions. High level answers and proposed SLA wording (draft bullets) below; Jonas/Ben please chime in if I missed anything.

Measurement boundaries (proposed):
- "Request ingress": timestamp when request is received by the Redwood edge load balancer (this is the canonical start time).
- "Token generation complete": timestamp when the final token for the request has been emitted by the Redwood runtime to the streaming pipeline (canonical end time).
- p95 latency = 95th percentile of (token generation complete - request ingress) computed on rolling 5-minute windows per-region.

Why this approach: it captures the server-side work (including queueing, model execution, KV cache lookups) and is resilient to measurement jitter caused by customer last-mile networks. We will also surface client-observed metrics separately if you want to correlate.

Exclusions (proposed language):
- Planned maintenance with >=30 minutes advance notice provided via the agreed change window process.
- Customer-initiated bulk batch jobs when explicitly tagged in the traffic sample and executed outside of declared peak windows.
- Third-party network outages (carrier-level issues) where telemetry indicates elevated packet loss or routing failures.

Remedies (proposed draft):
- Tier A breach: P95 breach > 2% of measured windows in a 30-day period => 5% credit of monthly invoice for impacted region.
- Tier B breach: P95 breach between 2% and 5% of measured windows in a 30-day period => 10% credit.
- Tier C severe: P95 breach > 5% of measured windows in a 30-day period => 20% credit + mandatory remediation review within 10 business days.
- Credits are applied to the monthly invoice following validation; repeated breaches may trigger a service review and escalation path.

Pre-prod load tests: Redwood can run a controlled pressure test in a staging environment if Acme provides traffic samples and a target window. We require 5 business days lead time to provision dedicated capacity and run the runbook with ops on both sides. Tests will be limited to agreed QPS and concurrency to avoid cross-tenant impact.

Action items:
- Sam: share traffic CSV and tag bulk jobs.
- Redwood: update the SLA draft with the exact measurement event names above and a sample credit calculation for procurement.

Ben — can you draft the short example credit calculation (numbers for typical monthly invoice sizes) and attach to the SLA doc?
